parts.visual:
You finish using an app, and a single question pops up: 'On a scale of 0 to 10, how likely are you to recommend us to a friend or colleague?' This is the most famous metric in modern business.

The Math of Loyalty:
1. Net Promoter Score (NPS): A customer loyalty metric developed by Bain & Company.
2. The Categories: 
- Promoters (Score 9-10): Loyal enthusiasts who will fuel your growth.
- Passives (Score 7-8): Satisfied but unenthusiastic; easily stolen by competitors.
- Detractors (Score 0-6): Unhappy customers who will actively damage your brand.
parts.audio: NPS is calculated by subtracting the percentage of Detractors from the percentage of Promoters. A score above 50 is excellent. A score below zero means your customers actively hate your company.

questions.question: A customer gives your software an '8' on the NPS survey. How does the NPS system categorize this user?
options: As a 'Passive'. They like the product, but they do not love it enough to risk their own reputation by recommending it to a friend. Passives do not help your startup grow.
questions.correct_answer: As a 'Passive'. They like the product, but they do not love it enough to risk their own reputation by recommending it to a friend. Passives do not help your startup grow.
questions.explanation: In NPS, an 8 is basically a zero. Only 9s and 10s matter.

questions.question: Listen to the CEO reacting to a massive spike in 'Detractors' (scores 0-6). What must the company do immediately?
questions.tts_text: Our NPS just dropped to negative 10! The new update must have broken something critical. I want the product team calling every single person who gave us a '2' right now to find out exactly what they hate.
options: Close the Feedback Loop. Detractors are a massive warning siren. The company must proactively contact them, apologize, fix the issue, and try to convert their anger back into loyalty.
questions.correct_answer: Close the Feedback Loop. Detractors are a massive warning siren. The company must proactively contact them, apologize, fix the issue, and try to convert their anger back into loyalty.
questions.explanation: A vocal Detractor will write a bad review that costs you 10 future sales.

questions.question: Why is the exact phrasing 'How likely are you to recommend us?' so powerful?
options: Because it is a short sentence.

Because recommending a product requires putting one's personal reputation on the line. People will say they 'like' a bad product to be polite, but they will never recommend a bad product to a colleague.
Because it is required by law.
questions.correct_answer: Because recommending a product requires putting one's personal reputation on the line. People will say they 'like' a bad product to be polite, but they will never recommend a bad product to a colleague.
questions.explanation: Social risk is the ultimate lie detector.

questions.question: If your startup has an incredibly high NPS (e.g., 70+), what is the best marketing strategy?
options: Activate the Promoters. You have an army of people giving you 9s and 10s. You should immediately build a 'Referral Program' to incentivize them to actually bring their friends into the platform.
questions.correct_answer: Activate the Promoters. You have an army of people giving you 9s and 10s. You should immediately build a 'Referral Program' to incentivize them to actually bring their friends into the platform.
questions.explanation: Promoters are unpaid salespeople. Give them a commission.

pairs.match: Net Promoter Score; the ultimate metric of customer loyalty
Highly loyal enthusiasts who will actively recommend your product
Satisfied customers who are vulnerable to competitive offerings
Unhappy customers who can damage your brand through negative word-of-mouth
